CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION migration.search_names(p_name text)
RETURNS TABLE(name text)
LANGUAGE sql
SECURITY INVOKER
AS $$
  SELECT n.name
  FROM migration.names n
  WHERE n.name ILIKE p_name;
$$;
semantic_differences: SQL Server collation Turkish_CI_AS implements Turkish-specific case folding (notably the dotted/dotless I behavior: 'i' <-> 'İ' and 'I' <-> 'ı'). PostgreSQL's built-in case folding used by ILIKE/LOWER does not reproduce Turkish_CI_AS semantics for all Unicode characters. Therefore searches that rely on Turkish-specific case-insensitive matching (for example involving 'i', 'I', 'İ', 'ı') may return different results.
Collation ordering differences are not reproduced. If the original search relied on collation-based ordering or comparisons beyond simple case-insensitive equality, PostgreSQL may behave differently.

No changes to NULL handling, duplicates or result ordering have been introduced beyond using the SQL definition above; equivalence for those aspects is not guaranteed by this translation unless verified on concrete test cases.
output.explanation: This function implements a case-insensitive search for names in the schema-qualified table migration.names using PostgreSQL's ILIKE. SQL Server's Turkish_CI_AS collation provides language-specific case folding (notably the dotted/dotless I rules) which PostgreSQL's default case-insensitivity does not reproduce without additional extensions or custom collation configuration. Because the original requested Turkish_CI_AS behavior cannot be guaranteed for every Unicode input in plain PostgreSQL, this translation documents that semantic difference. The function returns the same column name text as requested. As required, no external DDL, settings or extensions are used. The contractual adaptation from an EXEC/StoredProc style search to a SQL function returning a result set is implemented by returning TABLE(name text).

La función traducida ejecuta una SELECT bajo el nivel de aislamiento por defecto de la sesión en PostgreSQL (normalmente READ COMMITTED) y por tanto no reproduce la posibilidad de lectura sucia ni el comportamiento de evitar bloqueos de lectura que WITH (NOLOCK) proporciona en SQL Server.
output.explanation: Esta rutina implementa la misma proyección de columnas (id integer) que la consulta SQL Server original. Sin embargo, la semántica de WITH (NOLOCK) no es representable en PostgreSQL sin cambiar el nivel de aislamiento o usar construcciones que alteren garantías transaccionales de la sesión (lo cual usted prohibió). Por tanto la implementación realiza un SELECT directo desde dbo.policies y conserva orden, duplicados y valores NULL tal como están en la tabla, pero no puede reproducir lecturas sucias ni el comportamiento de evitación de bloqueos de WITH (NOLOCK). Según las reglas del contrato, esto se declara explícitamente en semantic_differences y la equivalencia queda pendiente de verificación por ejecutor.
